title: Advice, to-infinitives, superlatives and adverb comparison
matching: Typed answers ignore letter case, extra spaces, apostrophe style and final . ! or ? punctuation. Accents and every other character count. Multiple-choice answers must match exactly.

lessons.title: Should for advice and need to for necessity
lessons.explanation: Use should plus the base verb to give simple advice: You should see a doctor. The negative is shouldn't (should not): You shouldn't eat so much sugar. Should is the same for every subject and has no to. Use need to for something necessary: I need to buy a ticket. Need to changes for he, she and it (she needs to leave) and uses don't or doesn't in negatives.

examples.en: You should see a doctor.
You shouldn't eat so much sugar.
I need to buy a ticket.

pt.title: Should para conselhos e need to para necessidade
pt.explanation: Use should mais a forma base do verbo para dar um conselho simples: You should see a doctor. A negativa é shouldn't (should not): You shouldn't eat so much sugar. Should não muda conforme o sujeito e não é seguido por to. Use need to para algo necessário: I need to buy a ticket. Need to muda depois de he, she e it (she needs to leave) e usa don't ou doesn't nas negativas.

lessons.title: To-infinitive after common verbs
lessons.explanation: After some frequent verbs the next verb takes to plus the base form: want to, need to, decide to, hope to, plan to, learn to, would like to. Examples: I want to learn English. She decided to move. We hope to see you soon. These verbs do not take -ing. Do not drop to, and do not put a past or -s form after it: not I want to learns.

examples.en: I want to learn English.
She decided to move.
We hope to see you soon.

pt.title: Infinitivo com to depois de verbos comuns
pt.explanation: Depois de alguns verbos frequentes, o próximo verbo aparece com to mais a forma base: want to, need to, decide to, hope to, plan to, learn to, would like to. Exemplos: I want to learn English. She decided to move. We hope to see you soon. Esses verbos não são seguidos por -ing. Não omita to nem coloque depois dele uma forma no passado ou com -s: não diga I want to learns.

examples.en: I want to learn English.
She decided to move.
We hope to see you soon.

lessons.title: Superlatives with the most and -est
lessons.explanation: Use the superlative to say that something is first in a group. Short adjectives add -est: the tallest, the oldest; with a final -y change to -iest: the happiest. Longer adjectives use the most: the most expensive. Use the before a superlative noun phrase unless a possessive replaces it: the best day, but my best friend. A few are irregular: the best, the worst. Use in or of for the group: the tallest in the class.

examples.en: She is the tallest girl in the class.
This is the most expensive hotel.
It was the best day of my life.

pt.title: Superlativos com the most e -est
pt.explanation: Use o superlativo para dizer que algo ocupa o primeiro lugar em um grupo. Adjetivos curtos recebem -est: the tallest, the oldest; nos terminados em -y, troque -y por -iest: the happiest. Adjetivos mais longos usam the most: the most expensive. Use the antes de uma expressão com superlativo, a menos que um possessivo o substitua: the best day, mas my best friend. Alguns são irregulares: the best, the worst. Use in ou of para indicar o grupo: the tallest in the class.

lessons.title: Comparing how actions are done
lessons.explanation: Compare actions with adverbs. Use as ... as for equal: She runs as fast as me. Use not as ... as for less: He doesn't drive as carefully as she does. Use more plus a long adverb or the -er form of a short one: more slowly, faster, harder, earlier. Irregular: well becomes better. After than use an object pronoun or a short clause: She speaks better than me.

examples.en: She runs as fast as me.
He drives more carefully than his brother.
She speaks better than me.

pt.title: Comparando como as ações são feitas
pt.explanation: Compare ações usando advérbios. Use as ... as para indicar igualdade: She runs as fast as me. Use not as ... as para indicar menor intensidade: He doesn't drive as carefully as she does. Use more mais um advérbio longo ou a forma com -er de um advérbio curto: more slowly, faster, harder, earlier. A forma irregular de well é better. Depois de than, use um pronome de objeto ou uma oração curta: She speaks better than me.
